meta.topic: Syncing Code: push, clone, pull & fetch

questions.question: Which command uploads your local commits to a remote repository?
questions.explanation: `git push` publishes your local branch commits to the specified remote repository.

questions.question: What does the `-u` flag do in `git push -u origin main`?

options.B: Sets the upstream tracking reference so future `git push` and `git pull` know which remote branch to target

questions.explanation: `-u` (or `--set-upstream`) links your current local branch to the remote branch, enabling shorthand `git push` and `git pull` later.

questions.question: Which command downloads an entire existing GitHub repository and its complete commit history to your computer?
questions.explanation: `git clone` copies the remote repository, sets up `origin` automatically, and checks out the default branch.

questions.question: What is the key difference between `git fetch` and `git pull`?

options.A: `git fetch` deletes files; `git pull` recovers them
options.B: `git fetch` downloads remote commits without merging them into your working files, while `git pull` downloads AND merges them immediately
options.C: `git fetch` only works on branches named main
options.D: They do the exact same thing

questions.explanation: `git fetch` is safe and non-intrusive. `git pull` executes `git fetch` followed immediately by `git merge`.

questions.question: Which mathematical formula accurately describes `git pull`?

options.A: git pull = git add + git commit
options.B: git pull = git fetch + git merge
options.C: git pull = git clone + git push
options.D: git pull = git checkout + git reset

questions.explanation: Running `git pull` is shorthand for fetching remote branch changes and then merging them into your active branch.

questions.question: Why might Git reject a `git push` with an error saying '[rejected - non-fast-forward]'?

options.B: The remote branch contains new commits that you do not have locally yet
options.C: Your commit message was too short
options.D: GitHub is running out of disk space

questions.explanation: Git prevents you from accidentally overwriting teammates' work. You must `git pull` the remote commits first before pushing.

questions.question: What should you do when a push is rejected due to remote changes?

options.B: Run `git pull` to fetch and integrate the new remote commits, then push again
options.D: Create a brand new GitHub account

questions.explanation: Pulling integrates the remote work into your branch, allowing you to push cleanly.

questions.question: When you clone a repository with `git clone https://... my-app`, what does the optional `my-app` argument specify?

options.B: The custom name of the local folder created for the project

questions.explanation: By default, Git names the folder after the repository name. Supplying a custom second argument names the folder whatever you specify.

questions.question: Why should a developer run `git pull` at the start of every workday?

options.B: To ensure their local branch includes all changes and bug fixes made by teammates before writing new code
options.C: Git commands expire after 24 hours without pulling

questions.explanation: Starting from an up-to-date base branch prevents painful merge conflicts later in the day.

questions.question: What is `git push --force` (or `-f`) and why is it dangerous on shared branches?

options.A: It speeds up uploading large images
options.B: It overwrites the remote branch history with your local history, potentially destroying teammates' committed work
options.C: It creates a backup copy of the repository
options.D: It is completely safe and recommended for everyday use

questions.explanation: Force pushing overwrites the remote repository regardless of other people's commits. Never force push to shared branches like `main`!
